Here is a summary of Alberto Carbonell's profile, experience, stack and projects:

**Profile:**
- **Name:** Alberto Carbonell
- **Title:** Senior Software Engineer — AI Agents & Full-Stack TypeScript
- **Location:** Spain · Remote
- **Tagline:** Senior engineer, 10+ years with TypeScript, Node.js and PostgreSQL. I build AI agents that do real work end to end.
- **About:** Senior engineer with 10+ years shipping production software in TypeScript, Node.js and PostgreSQL. Lately my focus has been building AI agents that handle real work end to end, wired into the tools and data a business already uses. With AI in the loop I ramp up fast on any new stack; what never changes is the fundamentals: clean design, tests and code that's easy to maintain.
- **Education:** Higher Technical Diplomas (CFGS) in Web Development, Multiplatform Development and Systems Administration at CIFP Rodolfo Ucha Piñeiro (A Coruña), 2010 — 2015.
- **Languages:** Spanish (Native), English (C1).

**Experience:**
- **CoverWallet (2019 — now):** Senior Software Engineer in Madrid / Remote. Insurtech platform integrating external insurance carriers into a single commerce flow. Highlights include leading cross-team projects end to end, integrating third-party insurance carrier APIs, introducing AI agents into the engineering workflow, and mentoring new hires. Stack: TypeScript, Node.js, React, Ruby on Rails.
- **M&GT Consulting (2016 — 2019):** Software Developer in Madrid. Built REST APIs in Node.js and web/mobile apps for large international clients; delivered blockchain solutions on Hyperledger Fabric and Ethereum. Stack: Node.js, REST, iOS, Android, Hyperledger Fabric, Ethereum.
- **Indra (2015 — 2016):** Software Developer in A Coruña. Java/Spring and Oracle PL/SQL for telecom clients; QA and hotfixes. Stack: Java, Spring, Oracle PL/SQL.

**Stack:**
- **AI / agents:** Claude, Grok, Open-source models (cloud and local via Ollama), Tool calling, MCP, Agent evals and monitoring.
- **Languages:** TypeScript, JavaScript, Ruby.
- **Backend & data:** Node.js, NestJS, Express, Next.js, REST, GraphQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB.
- **Infra:** Docker, Kubernetes, CircleCI, Vercel, Railway, Neon, GCP.
- **Frontend:** React, React Native, Angular.

**Projects:**
- **Fraud Detection Agent (offline-evals):** Reviews newly published events and organizers on an event ticketing platform and leaves an approve / reject / request-info recommendation, with its reasons, for a human admin. Graded autonomy: it auto-approves only on evidence verified in code, and web sources can hold a decision back but never approve it. Offline evals showed significant improvements in fraud detection accuracy and reduced false approvals. Stack: TypeScript, PostgreSQL, GCP.
- **Organizer Support Agent (coming-soon):** Answers event organizers' questions about sales, payouts and setup without human review, pulling live data from PostgreSQL and the payments API. Stack: TypeScript, Tool calling, MCP, PostgreSQL.
- **Portfolio Agent (personal-project):** Agent on my portfolio site that answers visitors' questions about my experience and projects in natural language. Also exposed as an MCP server so external agents can query it. Stack: TypeScript, Claude, MCP. Links to source code and eval report available on GitHub.

**Practices:**
- **Offline evals before shipping:** This site's agent records its eval cases against a real model and replays them in CI, with no model or network: a stale recording or an off-topic leak fails the build.
- **Graded autonomy, a human in the loop:** The fraud detection agent recommends and a human admin decides; it approves on its own only on evidence verified in code.
- **Cost and limits tracked:** A token budget per request, per-IP rate limits and a monthly spend cap on this site's agent; every eval report shows mean tokens, latency and cost per case.
- **Changes measured run over run:** Every eval run appends its metrics to a history, so a prompt, tool or content change that moves the numbers shows up next to the run before it.

Would you like more specific details about any of these areas?
